correctness.rationale: For each plant i the extinction indicator has E Ii=q^{d_i}, and E IiIj=q^{|Ni∪Nj|}, so Var X=∑q^{d_i}(1−q^{d_i})+2∑(q^{|Ni∪Nj|}−q^{d_i+d_j}). With exactly 3 plants, every pollinator belongs to one of seven nonempty plant-subset types (a,b,c,d,e,f,g); under degree matching, variance differences depend only on sorted union-size triple (n−a,n−b,n−c). Independent complete composition enumeration for 1≤n≤10 found 17,017 connected type vectors, 1,529 distinct same-dual-degree union-profile pairs; each difference after q=t/(1+t) substitution has integer coefficients of just one weak sign, ruling out all sign changes over entire q∈(0,1). At n=11 G=(4,4,0,0,2,0,1), H=(5,2,1,1,0,1,1) are connected, share plant degrees (3,5,7), pollinator type degrees (8,2,1), and mean q³+q⁵+q⁷. Independent exact symbolic expansion yields VarG−VarH=2q^6(1−q)^2(q³+q²−1), crossing uniquely once at reciprocal plastic constant q≈0.754877666. Finite enumeration is exhaustive under the justified seven-type parametrization, not sampling an infinite size class.
risk: The proof applies only to three plants and independent identical primary hazards. The finite cutoff does not classify n>11.

value.rationale: Three plant species give the smallest nontrivial setting with three pairwise coextinction covariances. Holding both guild-degree multisets fixed forces equal mean loss curves but exposes topology-sensitive covariance. The exact pollinator-number threshold 11 plus a unique algebraic hazard crossover answers a motivated finite structural robustness question beyond generic simulations.
risk: Not a demographic/ecological validation; omits correlated hazards, rewiring, and cascading extinctions.

limitations: Exactly three connected plants; all pollinators positive degree; pairwise degree-matched graphs; iid loss q∈(0,1).
No conclusion for arbitrary number of plants or correlated extinction.
